drafts.title: mount: remote rename can retarget an unrelated local open handle
drafts.body:
**Describe the bug**

With two mounts, a rename event from one mount can be applied by path to an unrelated open handle on the other. In our incident, closing the unrelated empty Git lock then wrote an empty entry over the destination ref.

**System Setup**

Linux; two weed mounts against one filer. [Recreate and include exact master, filer, mount commands, weed versions, OS, and sanitized filer.toml.]

**Expected behavior**

A rename from another client must not retarget a local handle for a different file.

**Additional context**

We reproduced the incident with a delayed invalidation worker in an older build; the scratch scripts were not retained. Current behavior needs a new reproduction before this report is submitted. Ducktape: https://github.com/agentydragon/ducktape/issues/7767
drafts.review: The timing-sensitive reproducer was not retained; rebuild it and verify on current upstream before filing.

drafts.title: mount: O_CREAT|O_EXCL is not exclusive across mounts
drafts.body:
**Describe the bug**

Two clients can both create the same lock path with O_CREAT|O_EXCL when each has its own mount. In our setup the second create was checked against local metadata and the filer entry was deferred.

**System Setup**

Linux; two weed mounts on the same filer. [Supply exact version, commands, mount flags, OS, and sanitized filer.toml.]

**Expected behavior**

An exclusive create succeeds for at most one client, or the cross-mount limitation is clearly documented.

**Additional context**

A prior two-mount experiment reproduced both opens succeeding. Recreate the experiment on a current version and clarify whether -dlm changes the supported contract. https://github.com/agentydragon/ducktape/issues/7767
drafts.review: Recreate the two-mount test and check the advertised semantics and existing reports before filing.

drafts.title: bb remote retries an accepted run after a log-stream error
drafts.body:
**Describe the bug**

A log observation error after a remote run is accepted can cause bb remote to submit the entire command again. Side effects can repeat and the first run outcome may be unknown.

**To Reproduce**

Run a remote script with a visible side effect; after acceptance interrupt its log stream with an Internal/RST_STREAM failure. We observed a second outer invocation. [Add a minimal fault-injection harness and current-version result.]

**Expected behavior**

Reconnect to the accepted invocation or surface an outcome-unknown error instead of submitting it again.

**Desktop**

- OS: Linux
- Browser: not applicable
- Version: see additional context

**Additional context**

Observed with bb 5.0.498 on Linux. The client retry loop calls attemptRun again after a streaming logs error. Our detailed evidence and invocation links: https://github.com/agentydragon/ducktape/issues/13270. We currently use --disable_retry=true.
drafts.review: The observed failure is real; reproduce on the current CLI and check for duplicates before filing.

## Description

drafts.title: Terminating runner Pod on an unreachable node blocks reconciliation
drafts.body:
## Description

A runner Pod stuck terminating on an unreachable node can make every reconciliation time out while waiting for the same Pod to disappear.

## Reproduction

Start a runner, make its node unreachable and request deletion so it remains Running with a deletion timestamp. Reconcile repeatedly. [Provide a safe isolated reproduction and logs.]

## Expected behavior

Reconciliation has a bounded recovery strategy that accounts for a potentially still-running Terraform process and state lock.

## Environment and context

Observed on v0.16.5. Both the TLS-mismatch and terminating branches wait for NotFound. https://github.com/agentydragon/ducktape/issues/5704.

drafts.title: UpToDate peer pair retains nonzero out-of-sync bitmap after multi-peer recovery
drafts.body:
## Description

After a disk was reattached and one multi-peer resync completed, both peers reported UpToDate and Established while another connection retained a nonzero out-of-sync bitmap. Verification summary matched the pre-existing bitmap count; it does not establish the number of different blocks.

## Reproduction

Three diskful peers; detach and reattach one disk after storage exhaustion; observe a resync from one peer and a paused resync from another. [Reduce to a safe standalone reproduction; collect UUID, bitmap and state transitions.]

## Expected behavior

Replica state and pending reconciliation clearly reflect the remaining bitmap, or the expected semantics are documented.

## Environment and context

Observed with DRBD 9.3.3 and LINSTOR 1.35.2. Version 9.3.4 lists potentially related fixes; issue #149 describes a related but not proven identical resync stall. https://github.com/agentydragon/ducktape/issues/15010.
drafts.review: Do not file as confirmed data divergence. Reproduce on current DRBD and compare with existing issue #149.
